correctness.rationale: Every length-2m cyclic square in a two-b word has half b-count 0 or 1 because \(2m\le n\) and only two b positions exist. Zero b requires a block of 2m a within the longest a-gap. One b per half is possible iff the shorter oriented mark spacing \(r+1\)<=\(2m-1\), witnessed by choosing first-mark offset max(0,m-r-1). This proves both indicators for all \(p,q\ge0\); summation gives the parity formula and odd-length interval covering proves \(z_m\ge1\) and equality characterization. Independent exhaustive cyclic-factor enumeration agreed for all 3600 pairs with \(p,q<60\), checking all half-length type sets.

value.rationale: The 2026 source explicitly conjectures lower bounds on every prefix sum of half-length type counts for odd circular words. The present exact two-parameter four-run family proves the stronger termwise bound, gives the complete gap-resolved profile for arbitrary lengths, and identifies precisely the extremal balanced two-mark patterns. This is a motivated infinite-family structural subcase, not a narrow arbitrary finite enumeration or routine specialization of the known two-run proposition.
